newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle moderate at $65.00 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle moderate at $65.00 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Thursday traded in moderately active volume at $65.00 per cwt, steady with the bulk of this week's sales on Tuesday, according to feedlot sources.

Most of this week's showlists were sold Tuesday, but several feedlot managers Thursday reportedly were able to dip into next week's showlist to meet strong packer demand before frigid temperatures arrive at major feedlot areas.
About 16,700 head sold in the Panhandle, which brought the week to date total to 106,100, USDA said. In Kansas, about 12,400 head sold, for a weekly total of 102,600, USDA said.

Temperatures by this weekend were seen slipping to lows near zero degrees Fahrenheit in the Panhandle and below zero in Kansas, with wind chills ranging 30 to 60 degrees below zero. The cold air was expected to remain until midweek.
The cold could stress cattle and reduce weight gains, the feedlot sources said.
